title: introduce-rag-debugger-webview-inline-traces
author: Aisha Mehta
release_notes: Add an interactive RAG debugging webview for local development: inline trace annotations, step-wise execution, and a compact telemetry shim for reproducing session traces.
description: Motivation: Debugging retrieval-augmented generation sessions is hard when developers must iterate across prompts, retrieved chunks, and agent tool-calls. This PR introduces a lightweight webview-based RAG step debugger and an inline trace annotation format to make stepwise inspection and replay easy in local development. Changes: 1) new devtool - rag-debugger webview (Electron-friendly React SPA) that connects to the local quickstart via WebSocket; 2) trace annotation schema (.rt.jsonl) and an in-memory exporter used by the quickstart runner; 3) small SDK helpers in examples to emit span-like events for 'retrieve', 'score', 'tool_call', 'model_infer' with token-level offsets to enable inline highlights; 4) docs and quickstart script updates to show how to run the debugger and capture traces. Checklist: - [x] Implement webview UI with session list, step timeline, and inline document highlights - [x] Define minimal trace annotation schema and upgrade quickstart runner to optionally emit it - [x] Add SDK helper (examples/devtools/trace-client.ts) for instrumenting agents/tools - [x] Unit tests for schema validation and a snapshot test for the timeline UI - [x] Manual QA: reproduced known failing RAG flow from ENG-4821 and validated inline highlights. Commits summary: - feat(trace): add .rt.jsonl schema and serializer - feat(webview): add rag-debugger SPA and timeline components - feat(quickstart): wire websocket exporter and local runner flag --emit-trace - fix(tests): make deterministic timestamping for timeline snapshots - docs: add quickstart section + runbook for capturing traces Changed files (high-level): - examples/devtools/rag-debugger/* (new SPA and assets) - examples/quickstarts/local-rag-runner/index.ts (websocket exporter flag and wiring) - examples/devtools/trace-schema.rt.json (schema) - examples/devtools/trace-client.ts (helpers) - docs/quickstarts/debugging-rag.md (howto) - tests/trace-schema.test.ts (validation) - package.json (dev dependencies for bundling the webview) How it works (short): The quickstart runner can be started with --emit-trace to stream JSONL trace records to a local WebSocket; the webview connects, displays a session list with timestamps, and presents a step-by-step timeline. Selecting a timeline step shows the full prompt, retrieved documents (with inline highlight spans computed from offsets in the trace record), tool call input/output, and model logits/partial tokens when available. This enables deterministic step replay for debugging and easier root-cause analysis for retrieval failures or hallucinations. Backwards compatibility: Trace emission is opt-in and does not change produced outputs or callsites; schema is additive and namespaced under "rt." file extension. Migration notes: No runtime changes required for production deployments; examples only. Testing and QA: Unit tests validate schema and serializer; CI snapshot test exercises a recorded trace with the timeline renderer. Manual test: start quickstart with `npm run quickstart -- --emit-trace`, open `http://localhost:9876` served by the webview dev server, run the repro script in examples/repro/eng-4821 and step through timeline. Docs: New docs/quickstarts/debugging-rag.md contains setup steps, common troubleshooting, and a short list of live assertions to validate the trace mapping. Rollout: Merge into main and publish example build artifacts under examples/devtools/rag-debugger. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-4999 for a VS Code extension that embeds the same timeline and a follow-up for capturing opt-in telemetry to the staging observability stack. Notes for reviewers: focus on the schema safety boundary (trace-client.ts) and the websocket handshake in quickstart; both are intentionally minimal to avoid coupling to tooling. Security: traces are local-only by default; the quickstart explicitly warns in README about sensitive data and suggests redaction helpers in trace-client.ts.

review_comments: Jordan Li: Nice UX — can we collapse large tool outputs by default? Suggested adding a toggle — done in commit c4f902.
Tomás Rivera: Schema looks fine; please add strict validation for unknown fields to avoid version skew — addressed in serializer commit 3e7b1a.
Priya Kapoor: Confirmed local-only socket and README warning; please ensure no instrumentation is enabled by default — author reply: emission is opt-in and code paths gated behind --emit-trace flag.
ci_details: CI: lint ✓, unit tests ✓, bundle (webview) ✓, snapshot tests ✓. One intermittent e2e failed on network flake; rerun passed.
manual_qa: Reproduced ENG-4821 repro; used inline highlights to show missing document spans; timeline helped identify a retrieval scoring bug. Verified on macOS and Linux dev containers.
how_to_run: npm install && npm run build:webview && npm --prefix examples/quickstarts/local-rag-runner run start -- --emit-trace && open http://localhost:9876
notes: This PR is examples-only; follow-on work will extract the trace schema into a small npm package if the team wants to reuse across other quickstarts.
